notes: S319 audit. Every premise below was pre-verified against live code, live receipts, and live production HTTP before inclusion. The dominant finding (item 1) is a structural defect that explains the entire 12.3-day / 651-commit production dark period and was not previously filed on any surface: the hourly uptime-probe cron mutates five of the thirty-one leaves inside the promotion artifact AND re-renders the two receipts that judge that artifact, so the candidate/staging byte-match is destroyed and re-judged within the hour, every hour. An 8/8 release ceremony is unreachable by construction, independently of the Obelisk hold.

items.title: Stop the hourly telemetry cron from invalidating and then re-judging the release candidate
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED P0 — this is the structural cause of the 12.3-day production dark period, and it is filed on no existing surface. api/candidate-artifact-manifest.json enumerates 31 leaves; 5 of them (api/build-sha.json, api/public-intelligence.json, api/uptime.json, api/worker-route-provenance.json, assets/shell-manifest.json) were rewritten by automation crons between the staging deploy at 29be0bd8d and HEAD (git diff --name-only 29be0bd8d..HEAD over the leaf set). The same uptime-probe commit ALSO rewrites api/candidate-artifact-manifest.json and api/release-proof.json — the artifact and the receipt that judges it, in one commit. Observed live: three different roots for one unchanged source — staging 2cc84067…, release-proof candidate 0f89ab17…, recomputed-now a1bd0f91…. release-proof reports candidateReady:false, artifactManifest.matched:false, deployReceipt.attested:false ('receipt facts do not match current staging evidence'). Separately, scripts/generate-build-sha.mjs:34 writes builtAt: now.toISOString() — a wall-clock field inside a byte-checked artifact, so even a zero-source-change rebuild breaks the match. Byte-equality is only a valid gate when every input is reproducible where the check runs; here two independent inputs are not.
items.recipe: L2: split the promotion artifact into a reproducible source set and an observed telemetry set. Remove cron-owned and wall-clock-bearing paths from the artifact root computation, computing the root only over content whose bytes are a pure function of the commit; publish the excluded paths as a named, separately-versioned observedLeaves list on the receipt so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent. Drop builtAt from the hashed payload (keep it in a sibling non-hashed field). Add a self-test that mutates only an excluded leaf and asserts the root is unchanged, and one that mutates an included leaf and asserts the root changes.
items.conversionOutcome: A visitor reaches the current site: 651 commits of shipped fixes stop being unreachable because the promotion candidate survives longer than one cron tick.

L1.recipe: Exclude the five cron-owned leaves and the builtAt field from the hashed root; assert matched:true against the existing staging deploy.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a declared observedLeaves contract published on the receipt, plus two-way mutation self-tests proving the exclusion is exactly as wide as claimed.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a structural gate that fails any byte-checked artifact whose leaf set intersects a path written by a scheduled workflow or containing a wall-clock field — generalising the defect class (see item 8).

items.title: Give the production hold a blast radius instead of a boolean, so an identity dependency stops blocking unrelated surfaces
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED P0 — FOUNDER-GATED (AGENTS.md 'Escalate before changing: auth or security flows'). context/PRODUCTION_PROMOTION.json is a whole-site boolean (hold:true) whose single reason is real-provider-e2e-pending. That reason concerns one surface: the Worker identity plane at /auth/callback. api/release-dependencies.json shows the dependency is obelisk-staging-registration, ownerSlug 'obelisk' — a sibling repo, unsatisfiable from here under CANON-018. Meanwhile the hold blocks every unrelated surface: /stats/, /news/, /status/, the homepage, and 651 commits of content, performance and security work. This is NOT a request to bypass or hand-edit the hold, and it must not be implemented as one. It is a request to replace a coarse boolean with a resolved blast radius: a hold declares the surfaces it blocks; promotion of a surface set provably disjoint from every active hold's blast radius proceeds and publishes a receipt naming exactly what remains held. Anything the resolver cannot classify stays held — fail-closed, never fail-open.
items.recipe: L2: extend PRODUCTION_PROMOTION.json with a per-reason blastRadius path/route set. Build a resolver that maps a candidate promotion's leaf set to surfaces and refuses promotion on any intersection with an active hold, on any unclassifiable leaf, and on an empty/absent blastRadius (an unscoped reason keeps today's whole-site semantics). check-production-promotion-gate.mjs and run-release-ceremony.mjs read the resolver rather than the boolean. The public receipt publishes held surfaces by name so the trust surface gets more specific, not less. Mutation-test that adding an identity-plane leaf to the candidate flips the verdict to rejected.
items.conversionOutcome: Visitors receive twelve days of shipped fixes while the identity journey stays honestly held and named in public.

L1.recipe: Declare blastRadius for real-provider-e2e-pending and publish it on api/release-proof.json — reporting only, no gate change, so the founder can review the scope before it carries authority.

L2.recipe: L1 plus the fail-closed resolver wired into the promotion gate and ceremony, with disjointness proven per-leaf and mutation tests both ways.

L3.recipe: L2 plus per-surface promotion receipts and an independent re-verification that the held surface's bytes on production are unchanged after a scoped promotion.

items.title: Structural gate: no non-reproducible input may enter a byte-checked artifact
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED. Item 1 is one instance of a defect class this repo has now hit repeatedly: a --check gate that re-renders from a volatile input always drifts, and a byte-equality assertion is only valid when every input is reproducible where the check runs. Today nothing detects the class. The two live instances are a wall-clock field (scripts/generate-build-sha.mjs:34 builtAt) and cron-owned paths (uptime-probe.yml writing 5 of the 31 promotion leaves). A structural gate beats fixing the two instances, because the next byte-checked artifact will acquire a third.
items.recipe: L2: build scripts/check-artifact-reproducibility.mjs. Enumerate every byte-checked artifact's declared leaf set; cross it against (a) paths written by any scheduled .github/workflows/*.yml and (b) a scan for wall-clock expressions (Date.now, new Date().toISOString) in the producer of each leaf. Any intersection that is not on an explicit, justified allowlist fails. Wire it into build:check. Mutation-test on the real tree: re-adding api/uptime.json to the promotion leaf set must exit 1 naming that leaf and that workflow.
items.conversionOutcome: Release confidence stops silently decaying — a future promotion artifact cannot acquire an unpromotable leaf without a red gate.

L1.recipe: Detect wall-clock fields in byte-checked artifact producers only.

L2.recipe: L1 plus scheduled-workflow write-set cross-check and build:check wiring with real-tree mutation tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus modelling byte-checked artifacts in the evidence graph so a new artifact is auto-enrolled rather than hand-registered.

items.title: check-writeback-currency reports studio-ops' write-back debt from every sibling repo
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED, found live this session. vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/check-writeback-currency.mjs:33 sets ROOT = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..') and accepts no --project flag, so it always measures studio-ops regardless of cwd. The arc skill §2 F7 instructs every sibling repo to run exactly this command as its cut-off triage gate. Run here it emitted a ⛔ WRITE-BACK DEBT verdict citing commits 33a7fe77 / 9d6f584c / 93349673, none of which exist in this repository (git log -1 <sha> → 'unknown revision'). It is simultaneously a false positive in every sibling and a false negative for them: real sibling debt is invisible because the probe never looks at the sibling. The probe designed to catch collectively-stale surfaces is itself reading the wrong repo. CANON-018 forbids editing the sibling tree — this ships as Ark cargo.
items.recipe: L1: ship a pattern-share / repo-question cargo to studio-ops via scripts/ark.mjs proposing --project <path> (defaulting to process.cwd() rather than the script's own directory), with the observed evidence: the cited SHAs, the arc §2 F7 call site, and the both-ways failure mode. Record the local triage override in DECISIONS so this session's 'NOT cut off' verdict is auditable.
items.conversionOutcome: Every VaultSpark repo's arc triage stops reading another repo's ledger — no fabricated recovery work, no missed real debt.

L1.recipe: Ark cargo with evidence + local DECISIONS entry.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a proposed patch in the cargo payload and a self-test that runs the probe from a temp sibling and asserts it reports that sibling.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a studio-wide sweep for the same import.meta.dirname-rooted defect across every propagated probe.

items.title: One declared contract for api/build-sha.json, which today has two producers and two shapes
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED against live production. curl https://vaultsparkstudios.com/api/build-sha.json returns schemaVersion 1.1 with baselineSha, contentLaneHead and workflowRunId (written by .github/workflows/pages-deploy.yml:295). The repo builder scripts/generate-build-sha.mjs:34 writes schemaVersion 1.0 with none of those fields. A consumer reading baselineSha therefore gets it only after a content-lane deploy and silently gets undefined after a full build — the reader-keyed-on-a-field-its-producer-never-emits shape. Neither producer validates against the other.
items.recipe: L2: define one schema with the provenance fields optional-but-declared, emit it from both producers, and add a gate asserting the served artifact and the built artifact validate against the same schema and that every field a consumer reads is emitted by every producer.
items.conversionOutcome: Public build provenance means the same thing whichever lane deployed it, so /status/ cannot render a blank where a SHA belongs.

L1.recipe: Align generate-build-sha.mjs to 1.1 with nulled provenance fields.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a shared schema module and a producer/consumer field-coverage gate.

L3.recipe: L2 plus the same treatment for every dual-producer public artifact.
